affectedPublicSurfaces: Release CI (.github/workflows/pr.yml): a new isolation-proof job is APPENDED, hanging off the existing migration-check job which already stands up Postgres 16 and runs alembic upgrade head. This slice ships NO runtime code and NO migration — it adds a CI guard plus the isolation-proof harness and tests under the repo's test tree.

The isolation-proof harness itself: at test time it enumerates every table from pg_catalog / information_schema and classifies each via a small committed classification map (tenant-scoped-direct, tenant-scoped-via-parent, non-tenant). The map must be COMPLETE — an unclassified table fails the build — so the guard reads the catalog rather than a list that rots (ADR-061: the controls that survived were expressed as defaults, the ones expressed as conventions rotted; two tables landed unprotected during the audit that discovered the problem).

The standing guarantee for every future schema change: because coverage is the count of tenant-scoped tables in the catalog rather than a hand-maintained list, a table that lands unprotected lands the build red. This is the enforcement half of ADR-085 decision 3 — the reason #1328's policies cannot silently rot the way the previous RLS did.

candidateVerificationJourney.restrictedRoute: Not applicable to the running host — this slice ships no runtime code and no migration. The verification is entirely in CI: the isolation-proof job runs against a real Postgres 16, connected AS juli_app, with two seeded tenants, and asserts denial across every tenant-scoped table. The demonstrable proof for the PR is that the job runs RED against a deliberately-unprotected table (a table temporarily left unclassified or unprotected) and GREEN once it is protected/classified — both states shown in the PR. No public traffic, no candidate task set, no production credential or write is involved anywhere.
candidateVerificationJourney.notes: There is no host-side candidate journey because nothing runs on the host changes: the deliverable is a pr.yml CI job and its test harness. syntheticShopRequired is true for the two-tenant isolation seeding (distinct users, shops and a full row set across every tenant-scoped table); no real merchant data is touched. The job hangs off migration-check, which already provisions Postgres 16 and runs alembic upgrade head, so the isolation proof runs against the fully-migrated schema as juli_app. The DATABASE_URL cutover to juli_app on the deployed host is gate #1339 observation 1 — an owner act, entirely outside this slice.

journeys.name: catalog-enumerated-isolation-proof-red-then-green
assertions: the job runs against real Postgres 16, connected AS juli_app (never SQLite, never as the owner postgres); a test that merely asserts pg_policies is non-empty is explicitly NOT the mechanism and must not appear as the proof

every table is enumerated from pg_catalog / information_schema at test time and classified via the committed map; the count of covered tenant-scoped tables is asserted EQUAL to the count of tenant-scoped tables in the catalog, so a table cannot be skipped by being forgotten
the test of the test: a table CREATED inside the test transaction and left unclassified FAILS the proof — if the enumeration cannot see a new table it is a list wearing a query's clothing
with two seeded tenants and tenant A's context set as juli_app, SELECT, UPDATE and DELETE reach ZERO of tenant B's rows across every tenant-scoped table, and an INSERT of a B-owned row is rejected
the owner-bypass contrast is asserted: the same queries as postgres see BOTH tenants' rows, as juli_app see only tenant A's

the unset-context case is asserted in BOTH directions: zero rows from SQL (missing_ok=true), AND a named Python error from #1327's unit-of-work assertion — because if only one is proven the other is the failure mode that reads to a seller as 'you have no data'
the job is fail-closed: a database it cannot connect to, a classification map it cannot parse, or a table it cannot classify all FAIL the build — none of them skip
runtime is bounded and STATED; if the generated matrix exceeds the stated budget the fix is a tighter representative row set, never skipping tables
demonstration for the PR: the job is shown RED against a deliberately-unprotected table and GREEN after it is protected — proving the guard actually denies rather than merely existing

htmlRoutes: No HTML route, page, bundle, or static asset changes — the diff is one appended pr.yml CI job plus the real-Postgres isolation-proof harness and tests.

migrationCompatibility.notes: No migration and no runtime code in this slice — it adds a CI job and its test harness only. The job hangs off the existing migration-check job (Postgres 16 + alembic upgrade head) and runs the isolation proof against the fully-migrated schema as juli_app. Because it introduces no schema change, stable and candidate are trivially compatible; the guard's value is that every FUTURE migration is now checked for isolation coverage against the catalog rather than a list.

rollbackAssertion.preCutoverFailureBehavior: Do not merge. This slice ships no runtime code, no migration, and nothing that reaches the deployed host — it adds a CI guard. Until it merges, the isolation coverage is simply unchecked in CI (the status quo before this slice); there is no new exposure and no data hazard.
rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: Removing the job removes a guard and nothing else — no runtime behaviour changes. Removal must NOT be silent: the job is recorded in the runbook's list of required checks, so its absence is visible. Reverting the slice restores the prior (unchecked) CI state; no schema or data is touched either way.

acceptanceCommands: DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres@localhost:5432/juli_exec_1329 PYTHONPATH=$PWD/backend/src python -m pytest tests/integration -k 'isolation or catalog or tenant' -q
ruff check backend tests && ruff format --check backend tests
doNotInfer: The proof reads the catalog (pg_catalog / information_schema) at test time, NEVER a hardcoded table list. ADR-061 recorded that this repo lost RLS twice because remedies expressed as lists rotted while defaults survived; a list wearing a query's clothing is the exact failure to avoid.

The classification map must be COMPLETE: an unclassified table FAILS the build. The test of the test is a table created inside the test transaction and left unclassified — it must fail the proof, proving the enumeration actually sees new tables.
The count of covered tenant-scoped tables is asserted EQUAL to the count of tenant-scoped tables in the catalog, so nothing is skipped by being forgotten.

Connects AS juli_app to a REAL Postgres 16, never SQLite and never as the owner (postgres). Asserting pg_policies is non-empty is EXPLICITLY INSUFFICIENT and must not be the mechanism — the proof is DENIAL: SELECT, UPDATE and DELETE reach zero of tenant B's rows and INSERT of a B-owned row is rejected, across every tenant-scoped table.

The owner-bypass contrast is asserted (both tenants visible as postgres, only tenant A as juli_app), and the unset-context case is asserted in BOTH directions: zero rows via SQL AND a named Python error from #1327's assertion.

The job is fail-closed: an unconnectable database, an unparseable classification map, or an unclassifiable table all FAIL — none of them skip. Runtime is bounded and STATED; exceeding the budget is fixed with a tighter representative row set, never by skipping tables.

APPEND the pr.yml job — NEVER string-replace into an existing needs: block. Duplicate '- <job>' entries make a replace hit the wrong job, and an empty needs.X.result is the silent symptom; run the workflow validator after editing pr.yml. Hang the job off the existing migration-check job (Postgres 16 + alembic upgrade head). W6 is adding jobs in parallel, so keep the diff to appended blocks and do not touch W6's jobs.
This slice ships no runtime code and no migration; it must not perform, schedule, or partially apply the gate #1339 observation-1 DATABASE_URL cutover, and it does not edit any W6-owned file.
